text:
William Nylander has 11 goals and 22 points in 19 games, and he's moving up the Leafs' all-time lists. He's also in a public tug of war with his coach. Yahoo Sports carried Jim Hiller's line on Nov. 6: "Spending Less Time In The Neutral Zone Waiting For The Puck."

Our numbers explain why Hiller is pushing. At 5v5 Toronto gets just 40.9% of the expected goals with Nylander on the ice, 8 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had the same flaw last season: opponents got more chances with him out there than with nearly any other forward.

Meanwhile the scoring is running hot. He has 11 goals on 7.6 expected, and the Leafs have scored 6.5 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Nine of his points came on the power play. Toronto has lost three straight, the last a 4-0 night against New Jersey. If the finishing cools before the defense improves, this argument gets louder.
headline: Nylander scores, the coach wants more
